newsitem.title: INDIA: Vietnam floods unlikely to boost Indian rice sales.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam floods unlikely to boost Indian rice sales.

text.p: India's rice exports are unlikely to get a boost from an anticipated rise in prices of Vietnamese rice after substantial flood damage, traders said on Thursday.

Traders in Vietnam said their rice export prices were expected to rise sharply next month following serious floods damage to the country's main rice growing area. They said about 500,000 tonnes of rice was expected to be lost due to floods.
But Indian rice exporters said any rise in Vietnam prices was unlikely to boost their own sales.
"I don't think it is going to boost Indian rice exports," Prem Garg, a leading New Delhi exporter, said. "I don't think their (Vietnam traders') prices will in any case go above ours."
Traders said high Indian non-Basmati rice prices have forced overseas buyers to look towards Pakistan and Vietnam.
"Export demand for non-Basmati rice is not there as we are not competitive with Vietnam and Pakistan," Rashmi Bhimjayani, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.

Traders said export demand was expected to rise once Indian prices ease after new crop arrivals start picking up in September. "Demand will pick up as prices would fall by $10 to $15 when the new crop hits the market," Bhimjayani said.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $295-305 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $285-295, 15 percent at $270-280 and 25 percent at $250-260 per tonne.
Exporters said demand for India parboiled rice continued strong, mainly from Nigeria, South Africa and Saudi Arabia.
"The demand for 100 percent broken non-Basmati rice also continued to be strong but cargoes are not available," said Garg.
Traders said export shipments were affected by monsoon rains and port congestion. "Indian ports are getting crowded," Bhimjayani said.
"Robust demand for Basmati rice continues from the United States, the Middle East and some European countries," said another New Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Trade officials said Indian Basmati rice for export was currently quoted at $1,100 per tonne FOB, against about $900 at the same time last year.
Exporters said Iran was keen to buy Indian non-Basmati rice but was insisting on better quality of grain.
"They (Iran) are interested in buying our rice but we are not able to meet their specifications," Bhimjayani said. "Therefore only small contracts are being signed."
Traders said small quantities of new crop had started arriving in the local markets.
India harvested 80.54 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June), up from 79.62 million in the previous year. The government has not made a rice output forecast for 1997/98.
